processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50 kg ingot prepared by vacuum melting
forged into a billet with a cross-section of 30 mm × 30 mm
hot-rolled to a final thickness of 4 mm
designated 600-6; intragranular κ-carbides coarsen to ~18 nm with concurrent observable intergranular κ-carbide precipitation

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix with intragranular κ-carbides (~18 nm) forming well-defined arrays aligned along <100>, and observable intergranular κ-carbide precipitation at grain boundaries

phases_present.morphology: intragranular rectangular parallelepipeds forming well-defined arrays aligned along orthogonal <100> directions of the matrix; intergranular precipitation also observable at grain boundaries

precipitates.distribution: uniformly precipitated within austenite grains; well-defined arrays aligned along orthogonal <100> directions of the matrix

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: moving dislocations shear coherent ordered intragranular κ-carbides, creating anti-phase boundaries and enhancing glide plane softening and slip reversibility

interfaces.slip_behavior: planar dislocation slip induced by intragranular κ-carbides via glide plane softening; cross-slip suppressed and slip reversibility enhanced
interfaces.phase_evolution: aging at 600 °C for 6 h coarsens intragranular κ-carbides to ~18 nm and makes intergranular κ-carbide precipitation observable

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone, gauge width 5 mm, thickness 2.5 mm, R13 mm shoulder, tensile axis parallel to rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: universal testing machine Shimadzu AG-Xplus 250 kN; sample surfaces mechanically polished and electropolished (8 vol.% perchloric acid in ethanol, 30 s, 25 V)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone, same dimensions as tensile samples, loading axis parallel to rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: stress-controlled tension–tension, sinusoidal waveform, frequency 20 Hz, stress ratio R = 0.1; servo-hydraulic Shimadzu EHF-EV050K2A-020-1

fatigue_properties.fatigue_limit: 175.5 MPa (fatigue strength at 10^7 cycles without failure)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: best overall mechanical performance among aging conditions (high tensile strength + superior fatigue strength and fatigue life)
highest fatigue strength (175.5 MPa) among all conditions at low stress amplitudes

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: foils mechanically ground to ~50 μm then twin-jet electropolished in 8 vol.% perchloric acid in ethanol at 30 V; electrolyte at approximately -20 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize κ-carbide precipitation in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: intragranular κ-carbides ~18 nm, rectangular parallelepipeds aligned along <100>; intergranular κ-carbide precipitation observable

characterization_methods.technique: EBSD (BC, IPF, KAM, Schmid factor maps)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TESCAN MIRA3 SEM with Oxford EBSD detector; step size 0.8 μm; AZtecCrystal software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: acquired adjacent to main cracks at a stress amplitude of 225 MPa
characterization_methods.key_findings: transgranular crack along slip bands ({111} planes); moderate KAM levels with more diffuse misorientation distribution around crack tip; greater path tortuosity and microbranching than ST

characterization_methods.purpose: examine fracture surfaces and lateral surfaces of post-fractured samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: fΔ = 0.74 at 180 MPa (largest area fraction) and fΔ = 0.43 at 315 MPa; rapid fracture zone dimple-dominated (ductile microvoid coalescence); fatigue striations fine/dense

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: foils extracted from gauge sections of deformed specimens; fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 and 315 MPa
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize deformation microstructures in post-fractured samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: uniformly distributed planar slip bands with substantially lower overall dislocation density than ST at both 180 and 315 MPa

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and 315 MPa
characterization_methods.key_findings: distinct uniformly spaced planar slip bands at both 180 and 315 MPa; at 315 MPa spacing decreases with cooperative activation of multiple slip systems

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: fitted to stress-controlled tension-tension fatigue data in the finite-life region; RMSE of log10 Nf = 0.1776

unmapped_findings: fΔ (area fraction of crack initiation + propagation zones) = 0.74 at 180 MPa (largest among all samples at 180 MPa); = 0.43 at 315 MPa (source: b0041, figure_006).
Fatigue striation morphology for 600-6: at 180 MPa fine striations overlain by a fan-like vein/rib pattern; at 315 MPa dense parallel striations (source: figure_007).
Rapid fracture zone of 600-6 fails by microvoid coalescence (dimple-dominated ductile fracture) at both 180 and 315 MPa (source: b0043, figure_008).

Among aged samples, the intermediate intragranular κ-carbide size (~18 nm) of 600-6 achieves the highest fatigue strength due to a favorable balance of shearing-related strengthening and uniform planar slip (source: b0074).

At high stress amplitudes, fatigue life ranking among aged samples is 550-6 best, 600-6 intermediate, and 650-6 poorest, tracking the increasing severity of intergranular precipitation (source: b0080).
